definitions.explanation: Large-scale social or political disorder, including riots, revolts, and periods of instability. Often used to describe historical periods of conflict or significant social disruption.

examples.japanese: {国内|こくない}が{動乱|どうらん}に{陥|おちい}る。
{幕末|ばくまつ}の{動乱|どうらん}を{描|えが}いた{小説|しょうせつ}を{読|よ}んだ。
examples.english: I read a novel depicting the turmoil at the end of the Edo period.

examples.japanese: {政治的|せいじてき}な{動乱|どうらん}が{続|つづ}き、{多|おお}くの{市民|しみん}が{国外|こくがい}へ{避難|ひなん}した。
examples.english: Amid ongoing political upheaval, many citizens fled the country.

notes: A literary and formal word often found in news reporting and historical writing. Common collocations: {動乱|どうらん}の{時代|じだい} (era of turmoil), {動乱|どうらん}に{陥|おちい}る (to fall into turmoil), {政治的|せいじてき}{動乱|どうらん} (political upheaval). The {朝鮮動乱|ちょうせんどうらん} is a formal Japanese name for the Korean War. Compare with {混乱|こんらん} (confusion, disorder — more general and milder) and {暴動|ぼうどう} (riot — a specific violent act).
